Family: Amblycipitidae

Size: 4.5 cm

Temperature: 18-22°C

pH: 6.5-7.5

Vertebrae: 41-43.

Differs from all Indochinese species of Amblyceps in having a narrow head (9.5-11.1% SL versus 13.1-21.2) with a strongly projecting lower jaw (versus non- or weakly-projecting, except in A. platycephalus), and a very slender, elongate body (body depth at anus 7.6-11.1% SL versus 11.2-16.9 except in A. caecutiens) with 41-43 (versus 34-41) vertebrae.

Colouration: Olive brown body, lighter below.
Asia: India, Assam, Khasi Hills. Type locality: Kasyah mountains, India. The species' distribution in India and Bangladesh is estimated at around 40,000 km².
It is found in river beds with huge boulder outcrops at the base of hills.

Etymology: The specific name laticeps means "wide or broad head", although the description mentions A. laticeps as having a narrow head in relation to other species in this genus.

IUCN Red List: The population size and trend remain unknown, as this species is only known from scanty museum records. There is also very little information on its biology and the potential impacts of threats. Although Menon (2004) regarded this species as endangered, that assessment was based on incomplete information about its distribution. Its distribution is estimated at around 40,000 km², which makes it Least Concern until further information is available (IUCN 2010).
